sections.what_happened: IRGC Navy (early Monday statement): a tanker exiting the strait via the 'unauthorized southern route' with positioning/navigation systems switched off struck a naval mine, engine-room explosion and fire. AA details: Saturday's supertanker carried 2M+ barrels; third tanker Monday = third such incident in ~48h. US/Iran June MoU on freedom of navigation stalled over security disagreements.
sections.what_verified: AA, IRNA English, AFP wire (tribune.net.ph), Economic Times, NDTV, nukta, muslimnetwork. Ozmaei warning earlier in week corroborated.
sections.what_disputed: JMIC assessment: IRGC's Oct 17 tanker claims 'unsubstantiated'. Tanker identities and casualties undisclosed by Iran. DeepDraft raised Arabian Gulf threat to SUBSTANTIAL (1700-04). No independent/third-party verification of mines.
sections.why_matters: Three tankers in 48 hours, and every one of them had its transponder off. Iran's Hormuz regime is now: identify yourself or hit the mines. Washington's counter-blockade made this a war of attrition on the water — and oil markets are the casualty.
sections.context: Background: Gulf shipping — AA corroborates IRGC third-tanker mine claim; Saturday supertanker carried 2M+ barrels (VERIFICATION UPDATE, extends 1500-04, 1600-04, 1700-04, 1900-05)

totw_analysis: Our read: Three tankers in 48 hours, and every one of them had its transponder off. Iran's Hormuz regime is now: identify yourself or hit the mines. Washington's counter-blockade made this a war of attrition on the water — and oil markets are the casualty. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Mining your own blockade zone: legitimate coastal defense against sanctions-busters — or deliberate escalation of the world's most important oil chokepoint?
